## `[keys]`

One binding per line: a key sequence, then the command. The last word on the line is the
command and everything before it is the key sequence, so keys such as "=" need no quoting.
The command "none" removes a binding. Later lines win: binding a sequence removes the
bindings it conflicts with (binding C-x would remove every C-x ... binding), with a warning.

Key notation, as Emacs' kbd:

```text
  C- Ctrl, M- Alt (Meta), S- Shift, combined in any order: C-M-<home>.
  A character: a  5  /  {  ;  and so on. SPC is the space bar.
  Named keys: RET TAB ESC DEL (Backspace) <delete> <insert> <home> <end> <prior> (Page Up)
  <next> (Page Down) <left> <right> <up> <down> <f1> ... <f24> <pause> <apps>.
  A sequence is up to 4 keys separated by spaces: C-x C-s.
```


Keys match by the character they type in the current keyboard layout: C-/ is Ctrl with
whatever key types "/". Shift is part of the character for everything except letters, so
Ctrl+Shift+/ on a US keyboard is C-? and letters keep it as a modifier: C-S-a. A key with
Shift and no binding runs the binding it has without Shift. Plain characters can be bound
too (they then stop inserting themselves); the second key of a sequence often is one (C-x o).
Because '#' starts a comment, a lone "#" key cannot be bound (M-# can).

| keys | command | what it does |
|---|---|---|

## `[keys minibuffer]`

While the minibuffer reads something (M-x, C-x C-f, ...), these bindings come first; every other
key falls through to [keys] above, so all editing commands work in it. C-g and ESC abort any
prompt, including the y / n questions, whose other keys are taken as answers.
RET takes the selected candidate (or the input when there is no list), C-j the input exactly as
typed. TAB completes to the longest common part, then to the selection. Candidates match when
every space-separated word of the input occurs in them, ignoring case.

<!-- keymap: minibuffer -->
| keys | command | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `RET` `C-m` | `exit-minibuffer` | Accept the selected candidate or the input |
| `C-j` | `exit-minibuffer-input` | Accept the input exactly as typed |
| `C-g` `ESC` | `abort-minibuffers` | Abort the prompt and the commands waiting on it |
| `M-p` | `previous-history-element` | Use the previous input from the prompt's history |
| `M-n` | `next-history-element` | Use the next input from the prompt's history |
| `DEL` | `minibuffer-backward-updir` | Delete back a character, or a directory after a slash |
| `TAB` `C-i` | `minibuffer-complete` | Complete the input to the longest common part |
| `C-n` `<down>` | `minibuffer-next-completion` | Select the next candidate in the list |
| `C-p` `<up>` | `minibuffer-previous-completion` | Select the previous candidate in the list |
| `<next>` | `minibuffer-next-page` | Select the candidate one page down the list |
| `<prior>` | `minibuffer-previous-page` | Select the candidate one page up the list |

## `[keys search-results]`

In a results buffer (*search*, *occur*) these bindings come first. RET visits the match on its line
in another window and selects it; n and p show the next and previous match in another window and
stay in the results; g runs the search again; q closes the results window.

<!-- keymap: search-results -->
| keys | command | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `RET` `C-m` | `compile-goto-error` | Visit the location on this results line |
| `n` | `next-error-no-select` | Show the next location in another window |
| `p` | `previous-error-no-select` | Show the previous location in another window |
| `g` | `recompile` | Run the last build or search again |
| `q` | `quit-window` | Quit the results window |

## `[keys compilation]`

In *compilation* these bindings come first: RET, n, p and q as in a results buffer (the lines with a
location; n and p skip notes), g runs the command again, C-c C-k kills it.

<!-- keymap: compilation -->
| keys | command | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `RET` `C-m` | `compile-goto-error` | Visit the location on this results line |
| `n` | `next-error-no-select` | Show the next location in another window |
| `p` | `previous-error-no-select` | Show the previous location in another window |
| `g` | `recompile` | Run the last build or search again |
| `q` | `quit-window` | Quit the results window |
| `C-c C-k` | `kill-compilation` | Stop the running build |

## `[keys command-list]`

While the command list (C-S-p) is open these bindings come first. Typed characters and the line editing
commands (C-a, C-e, C-f, C-b, M-f, M-b, DEL, C-d, C-k, M-DEL, C-w, M-w, C-y, M-y, C-/ ...) edit the
filter; any other command is refused while the list is open. C-g, ESC or a click outside close it.
A click selects a row, a double click runs it, the wheel scrolls.

<!-- keymap: command-list -->
| keys | command | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `C-n` `<down>` | `modal-next` | Select the next row of the open modal |
| `C-p` `<up>` | `modal-previous` | Select the previous row of the open modal |
| `C-v` `<next>` | `modal-next-page` | Select the row one page down in the open modal |
| `M-v` `<prior>` | `modal-previous-page` | Select the row one page up in the open modal |
| `RET` `C-m` | `modal-accept` | Accept the selected row of the open modal |

## `[keys git-changes]`

While the git changes view (C-x g) is open these bindings come first; any other command is refused.
The movement keys select a file on the left (its diff is fetched once) or, after TAB, scroll the diff
on the right; TAB goes back. RET visits the selected file at its first change, g runs git status
again, C-g, ESC or a click outside close the view. The wheel scrolls the pane under the pointer.

<!-- keymap: git-changes -->
| keys | command | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `C-n` `<down>` | `modal-next` | Select the next row of the open modal |
| `C-p` `<up>` | `modal-previous` | Select the previous row of the open modal |
| `C-v` `<next>` | `modal-next-page` | Select the row one page down in the open modal |
| `M-v` `<prior>` | `modal-previous-page` | Select the row one page up in the open modal |
| `RET` `C-m` | `modal-accept` | Accept the selected row of the open modal |
| `TAB` | `modal-other-pane` | Move the focus to the next pane of the open modal |
| `g` | `git-changes-refresh` | Run git status again in the git changes view |

## `[keys isearch]`

While an isearch is active these bindings come first. Typed characters extend the search string;
a key bound to any other command ends the search at the match and then runs that command. A
search string without capital letters matches either case, one with a capital letter matches
exactly (M-c switches). Repeating at the last match wraps around the buffer. RET and ESC end the
search at the match and set the mark where it started; C-g goes back there (or, while the search
is failing, first removes the part that is not found).

<!-- keymap: isearch -->
| keys | command | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `C-s` | `isearch-repeat-forward` | Search for the next match of the search string |
| `C-r` | `isearch-repeat-backward` | Search for the previous match of the search string |
| `DEL` | `isearch-delete-char` | Undo the last change to the search string |
| `RET` `C-m` `ESC` | `isearch-exit` | End the search at the current match |
| `C-g` | `isearch-abort` | Abort the search and go back to where it started |
| `C-w` | `isearch-yank-word` | Add the next word of the buffer to the search string |
| `C-y` | `isearch-yank-kill` | Add the last kill to the search string |
| `M-p` | `isearch-ring-retreat` | Use the previous search string from the history |
| `M-n` | `isearch-ring-advance` | Use the next search string from the history |
| `M-c` | `isearch-toggle-case-fold` | Toggle case sensitivity of the search |

## Commands without a default key

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `self-insert-command` | Insert the character of the key that was typed |
| `revert-buffer` | Revert the buffer to its file's contents on disk |
| `recover-file` | Recover a file from its crash recovery copy |
| `set-language` | Set the buffer's language for highlighting |
| `set-theme` | Switch the colors to another theme for this session |
| `replace-string` | Replace a text from point without asking |
| `project-find-file-other-window` | Find a project file and open it in another window |
| `project-refresh` | Scan the project's files again |
| `compile` | Run a build command in the buffer's directory |
| `skip-to-next-like-this` | Move the newest cursor to the next match of the region |
| `unmark-next-like-this` | Remove the newest cursor |
| `edit-ends-of-lines` | Add a cursor at the end of every line of the region |
| `edit-beginnings-of-lines` | Add a cursor at the start of every line of the region |
